title: Bribery-set odds invariant
statement: Let $n\ge 2$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be monotone with positive bias $p=\Pr[f(x)=1]>0$ under the uniform distribution. Fix a real target $q<1$. Starting from $J_0=\varnothing$, define $J_{t+1}$ by leaving $J_t$ unchanged if the uniform mean of $x\mapsto f(x^{J_t})$ is at least $q$, and otherwise adjoining to $J_t$ a coordinate of maximum influence for that function; here $x^{J_t}$ is obtained by setting every coordinate in $J_t$ to $1$. For every integer $t\ge0$, if $p_t=\Pr[f(x^{J_t})=1]$ and $r=\frac{\log n}{100n}$, then $(1+2r)^{|J_t|}p(1-p_t)\le p_t(1-p)$.
hypotheses_covered: $n$ is a natural number with $2\le n$
$f$ is a Boolean function on sign vectors of length $n$
The positive bias of $f$ is positive
